summary: Takatsugu Hayashi is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar who studied at the University of Delhi (Ph.D.). He held posts at Tohoku University, Sendai National College of Technology, Hosen Gakuen College, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takayasu Higuchi (1919–2015) studied at Kyoto University (~1939–1942), where he later served as professor of archaeology (~1953–1983). In his fields of history, archaeology, and Iranian/Central Asian studies, he directed Sen-oku Hakuko Kan, Sen-oku Matsurokan, Kashihara Archaeological Institute, and the Research Centre for Silk Roadology.

Takayasu Kimura (born 1934) works in Indology and Buddhist studies. He completed doctoral coursework at Taisho University and held posts at Taisho University (attested 1995) and the Institute of Modern Religious Education of Shingon Buzan (attested 1995).
Takayasu Suzuki (born 1964) is a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1989–1998) and served as a professor at Yamaguchi Prefectural University (~2004–2017).

Takayoshi Kamei (1886–1977) was a historian and Japanologist who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1908–1911). He held positions at the University of Tokyo (~1916–1946), Ibaraki University (~1950–1961), and Seisen University (~1961–1971).

Takayoshi Namikawa (born 1947) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned his degrees, including a doctorate in literature, at Bukkyo University, where he became professor in 1981 and professor emeritus in 2018. He also taught at Jawaharlal Nehru and Hokkaido universities.

Takayuki Hirosawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who studied at the University of Hamburg under Lambert Schmithausen. He has held positions as a group member and professor at Taisho University.

Takehiro Sueki (1921–2007) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1941–1944). He later held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1968–1982), Toyo University, and the University of Electro-Communications.

Takeo Hibino (1914–2007) was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University (~1933–1936). He held posts at Kyoto University and its Institute for Research in Humanities (1936–1977), Otemon Gakuin University (1977), and Otemae University (1980).

Takeo Kanaseki (1897–1983), who worked in history and archaeology, studied at Kyoto University (~1919–1923). He held appointments at Kyushu University (~1950–1960), Tottori University (~1960–1969), and Tezukayama Gakuin University (~1969–1979).

Takeshi Fujii (born 1955) is an Indology and history scholar who studied at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies and the University of Delhi. He spent his academic career at Tokyo University of Foreign Studies (1987–2021), rising from assistant to professor and professor emeritus.

Takeshi Hasegawa is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He has held posts at Ryukoku University (attested 1998), the International College for Postgraduate Buddhist Studies (attested 2026), and the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

Takeshi Karashima (1903–1967) was a Sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1924–1927). He held posts at Keijo Imperial University (~1928–1945), Showa Women's University (~1952–1960), Sagami Women's University (~1960–1967), and Kamakura's library.

Takeshi Umehara (1925–2019) was a philosopher and Japanologist who studied at Kyoto University under Tokuryu Yamauchi. He held posts at Ryukoku, Ritsumeikan, and Kyoto City University of Arts, and served as director of the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (1987–1995).

Takeshiro Kuraishi (1897–1975) was a scholar of Sinology and linguistics who studied at the University of Tokyo (~1918–1921). He was a professor at Kyoto University (~1939–1949), taught at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1958), and chaired the Chugokugo Gakkai.

Takezo Kaneko (1905–1987) was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo under Tetsuro Watsuji (~1926–1929). He served as a professor at the University of Tokyo (~1950–1966) and held posts at Hokkaido, International Christian, and Seikei universities.

Taklung Tsetrul Rinpoche (1926–2015) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology master who studied under Po Lu Khenpo Dorjé. Succeeding Trulshik Rinpoche Ngawang Chökyi Lodrö in 2012, he served as Supreme Head of the Nyingma school until 2015.
Taku Fukuda (born 1963) is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Hajime Sakurabe. He has held positions at Doho University, Nagoya University, and the Nakamura Hajime Eastern Institute.

Takudo Ishikawa specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He has held posts as a research fellow at the Jodo Shu Research Institute (attested 2005–2006) and as a faculty member at Taisho University (attested 2015, 2026).

Takushu Sugimoto (born 1935) studied at Tohoku University under Ensho Kanakura, Hakuyu Hadano, Teruji Ishizu, and Ichiro Hori, completing a PhD under Birendra Prasad Sinha. He held professorships at Kanazawa University, Komazawa University, and Kinjo University.
